analysis:
The supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1-797). The changed ranges are documentation only, at head lines 1087-1090, 1101-1159 and 2041-2060. The patch excerpt shows a scheduler-geometry table update in the production settings table: Gemma 4 gets a wide prefill chunk (2048 chunk / 4096 step), other families keep 512 / 2048, soloPrefillStripeTokens is per-family, and a bidirectionalMediaPrefillChunkCeiling of 512 is added. These rows only describe code in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift. That source is not supplied, and neither are the other changed head ranges (1101-1159, 2041-2060), so none of the underlying behavior was verified here.

Threat-model relevance: a wider Gemma 4 prefill chunk raises transient activation memory and per-step GPU occupancy, which touches the availability and resource-accounting concerns around TB-007 and T-029. A larger step also bears on in-flight cancellation granularity (T-010). The documented mitigations are existing byte-level admission, the activation reserve and the media prefill ceiling. Whether the implementation prices the wider chunk in the shared KV/process-memory ledger needs the code change to confirm. The patch also does not touch prefix-cache behavior, so the T-041 posture (SSD tier, HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, authenticated cache scope) is unchanged in the supplied text. The base text describes the Nemotron Super slot, cache scoping (tenant-partitioned, cold without a scope) and media admission. The changed lines do not alter any of that.

No security regression is identifiable from documentation-only changes, and no attestation, encryption, authorization or data-exposure behavior is altered in the visible evidence. Integration should check that the code behind the new prefill geometry (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift prefillGeometry) keeps memory admission and the media ceiling consistent with these documented values. The remaining head-side hunks should also be checked for claims that overstate security properties.
